neet_che_u04_t02_1.working: Enthalpy, entropy and Gibbs energy are state functions. Work depends on the path taken, so it is a path function.

neet_che_u04_t02_2.working: Over a complete cycle, every state function returns to its initial value, so ΔU, ΔH and ΔG are all zero. Heat q is a path function, so it need not be zero.

neet_che_u04_t02_3.working: Path 1: q = +50 J and w = -20 J, so ΔU = 50 - 20 = 30 J. ΔU is the same for path 2, so w = ΔU - q = 30 - 40 = -10 J.

neet_che_u04_t02_4.working: For an ideal gas, U depends only on T, so ΔU = 0 in an isothermal process and A is true. In an isothermal process heat is exchanged (q = -w), so R describes an adiabatic process and is false.

neet_che_u04_t02_5.working: Entropy is a state function, so ΔS = 0 over a cycle, while q and w can be non-zero; Statement I is correct. q + w = ΔU, which is a state function and path-independent; Statement II is incorrect.
